story: Amirani, a culture hero, was the son of Dali, a goddess of the hunt, but was removed prematurely from her womb and raised by a hunter named Sulkalmakhi and his wife Darejan, alongside her two natural sons, Badri and Usup. Raised violently in the wilderness, the three brothers attacked every stranger they met to test their strength. Eager for adventure, Amirani fought against Devs, demonic giants living at the edges of inhabited lands. Later, to avenge their murdered uncle, the brothers sought out his killer, a three-headed giant named Baq'-Baq'. Amirani challenged the giant and cut off all three heads; from each head a worm emerged and became a dragon—one white, one red, one black. Amirani killed the white and red dragons, but the black dragon swallowed him and fled to the Black Sea or the underworld. From inside, Amirani cut the dragon open and killed it. He then journeyed overseas seeking kamar, daughter of the demon king Kaji. The demon army killed his adopted brothers, but Amirani slew every enemy, including their king. Grief-stricken, he took his own life, but kamar used magic to revive him and his companions. Wandering alone, Amirani met an undead giant he could not lift. He prayed to Ghmerti (God), who granted him great strength, making him arrogant enough to challenge God to a duel. As punishment, God chained him beneath a mountain, guarded by his winged dog Q'ursha, whose licking of the chains was undone whenever distant blacksmiths struck their anvils. Once yearly the mountain opens, letting Amirani see the sky briefly before closing again.
